title: Severe bleeding and wounds
description: Heavy or uncontrolled bleeding from a wound. Rapid blood loss can be life-threatening.

recognition_questions.q: Is the bleeding heavy, spurting, or soaking through cloth?
Is the person responsive and oriented?
Is there an object embedded in the wound?

immediate_safety_warnings: Protect yourself from bloodborne infection — use gloves or a clean plastic bag if available.
Do not remove an embedded object — it is controlling the bleeding.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Call 112 (or ask someone to) if bleeding is heavy or spurting.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Severe bleeding can cause fatal shock within minutes.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Apply firm direct pressure on the wound with a clean cloth or gauze.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Pressure is the primary way to control bleeding.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If there is an embedded object, press firmly around the object, NOT on it.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Removing the object can worsen bleeding.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Keep pressure for at least 10 minutes without lifting the cloth to check.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Lifting the cloth disturbs the clot.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If blood soaks through, do not remove the cloth — add more layers on top and press harder.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Removing the cloth removes the clot.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If possible, raise the injured limb above the level of the heart (unless fractured).
ordered_instructions.rationale: Gravity reduces blood flow to the wound.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Help the person lie down and keep them warm to prevent shock.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Reduces the effects of blood loss.

actions_to_avoid: Do not remove an embedded object.
Do not use a tourniquet unless you are trained and bleeding is life-threatening on a limb.
Do not lift the cloth to check the wound.
Do not give food or drink (the person may need surgery).
Do not put powders, herbs, or home remedies on the wound.

escalation_conditions.condition: Bleeding not controlled after 10 minutes of firm pressure
Person becomes pale, cold, confused, or loses consciousness
escalation_conditions.action: Treat for shock; ensure 112 called; if unconscious and not breathing, start CPR

escalation_conditions.condition: Bleeding is spurting (arterial) or from a major wound

approved_alternatives.alternative: Clean plastic bag over the hands
Torn strips of cloth or a clean scarf

follow_up_requirements: All severe wounds need medical assessment.

age_specific_pathways.child: Use less pressure; reassure the child; same technique.
age_specific_pathways.infant: Apply gentle but firm pressure; watch for shock.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
